note: z/OS calibration probes (#4702 Part 2): our own fixed-format COBOL, runnable on Enterprise COBOL and on cobc -std=ibm. Run each on z/OS, record the result per entry in zos_calibration.json (key: probe id). oracle_expected is GnuCOBOL 3.1.2 -std=ibm output (gitgalaxy-gnucobol:3), measured 2026-10-22, DISPLAY lines in order. Never Hercules; results only after counsel clears licence and publishing (Q16). runtime_options: the effective LE / Db2 / CICS option set (RUNTIME_OPTION_TABLE keys, the IBM default each) the region must hold when a probe runs; a probe's runtime_variants each name keys to replace for one more run. Every recorded result carries the set it was measured under.

c1-trunc-std.question: MOVE 99999 to S9(4) COMP and ADD 1 to 9999 with ON SIZE ERROR: IBM stores 9999 and raises the size error
c1-trunc-std.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 B PIC S9(4) COMP.
       01 N PIC 9(6) VALUE 99999.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE N TO B
           DISPLAY "B1=" B
           MOVE 9999 TO B
           ADD 1 TO B
               ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "SE"
           END-ADD
           DISPLAY "B2=" B
           STOP RUN.
c1-trunc-std.note: Plain `cobc -std=ibm` behaves as TRUNC(BIN); the register's equivalence harness passes the TRUNC flag, so this row is the unflagged instrument, not the det port's answer.

c3-literal-truncated-to-zero.question: MOVE -1000 TO S9(3) (literal) and MOVE of the same value from a field: does the zero result keep its sign
c3-literal-truncated-to-zero.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P3.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 S PIC S9(3).
       01 M PIC S9(4) VALUE -1000.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE -1000 TO S
           DISPLAY "S1=" S
           MOVE M TO S
           DISPLAY "S2=" S
           STOP RUN.
c3-literal-truncated-to-zero.note: The oracle folds the literal MOVE to +0 and keeps the sign for the field MOVE.

c4-unsigned-binary-below-zero.question: SUBTRACT past zero from an unsigned binary: IBM keeps the absolute value
c4-unsigned-binary-below-zero.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P4.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 U PIC 9(4) COMP VALUE 3.
       01 Z PIC 9(4) COMP VALUE 0.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           SUBTRACT 5 FROM U
           DISPLAY "U1=" U
           SUBTRACT 1 FROM Z
           DISPLAY "Z1=" Z
           STOP RUN.
c4-unsigned-binary-below-zero.note: The oracle wraps; the det runtime follows IBM (C4, declared difference).

c13-edited-and-zoned-compare.question: Numeric-edited item against a number is compared as text; signed zoned item against an alphanumeric literal and against a number
c13-edited-and-zoned-compare.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P13.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 E PIC ZZZ,ZZ9.99 VALUE ZERO.
       01 Z PIC S9(4) VALUE -12.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE 1500 TO E
           IF E > 1499 DISPLAY "E1=GT" ELSE DISPLAY "E1=NGT".
           IF Z = "0012" DISPLAY "Z1=EQ" ELSE DISPLAY "Z1=NE".
           IF Z = 12 DISPLAY "Z2=EQ" ELSE DISPLAY "Z2=NE".
           STOP RUN.
c13-edited-and-zoned-compare.note: Confirms the Language Reference's comparison-by-operand-class table on z/OS.

c14-size-error-zero-divisor.question: DIVIDE by zero with ON SIZE ERROR and 0 ** -1 with ON SIZE ERROR
c14-size-error-zero-divisor.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P14.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 A PIC 9(4) VALUE 7.
       01 Z PIC 9(4) VALUE 0.
       01 R PIC 9(4) VALUE 55.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           DIVIDE A BY Z GIVING R
               ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "SE1"
           END-DIVIDE
           DISPLAY "R1=" R
           COMPUTE R = Z ** -1
               ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "SE2"
           END-COMPUTE
           DISPLAY "R2=" R
           STOP RUN.
c14-size-error-zero-divisor.note: IBM says 0 ** -1 is a size error (the oracle returns 0 and takes no size error). Run only the ON SIZE ERROR forms: a bare zero divisor can abend S0CB.

c2-intermediate-truncation.question: COMPUTE R = A / B * C with A = 1, B = 3, C = 300: IBM carries the quotient to dmax decimal places (2), so 0.33 * 300 gives 99, not 100
c2-intermediate-truncation.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P2.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 A PIC 9V99 VALUE 1.
       01 B PIC 9 VALUE 3.
       01 C PIC 999 VALUE 300.
       01 R PIC 9(4)V99.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE R = A / B * C
           DISPLAY "R1=" R
           STOP RUN.
c2-intermediate-truncation.note: The #4287 shape. Does not probe the 30-digit cap (the register's To-settle bullet is answered on the oracle only).

c11-nondigit-moved-to-zoned.question: MOVE an alphanumeric 1! to PIC 9(2) and test IS NUMERIC: the oracle gives 01 and NUMERIC; IBM documents no result for the non-digit
c11-nondigit-moved-to-zoned.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P11.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 X PIC X(2) VALUE "1!".
       01 N PIC 9(2).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE X TO N
           DISPLAY "N=" N
           IF N IS NUMERIC DISPLAY "NUM" ELSE DISPLAY "NOTNUM".
           STOP RUN.
c11-nondigit-moved-to-zoned.note: IBM side undefined under PFD. Record what z/OS does (observed), do not expect a match.

d2-hex-literal-charset.question: A PIC X item holding X"40": is it SPACE (EBCDIC) or @ (ASCII)
d2-hex-literal-charset.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P22.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 H PIC X VALUE X"40".
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           IF H = SPACE DISPLAY "H=SPACE" ELSE DISPLAY "H=OTHER".
           IF H = "@" DISPLAY "H=AT" ELSE DISPLAY "H=NOTAT".
           STOP RUN.
d2-hex-literal-charset.note: The oracle is ASCII, so it differs from z/OS by design (D2 declared difference); expected z/OS output is H=SPACE, H=NOTAT.

c5-packed-unsigned-sign-nibble.compile_options: NUMPROC(NOPFD) (IBM default); run again with NUMPROC(PFD)
c5-packed-unsigned-sign-nibble.question: A COMP-3 value 123 carrying the unsigned sign nibble F: ADD 1 GIVING M, then compare N with 123 and test M's stored sign. NOPFD accepts F and generates the preferred sign C in the receiver; PFD is not required to
c5-packed-unsigned-sign-nibble.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P5.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 RAW PIC X(2) VALUE X"123F".
       01 N REDEFINES RAW PIC S9(3) COMP-3.
       01 M PIC S9(3) COMP-3.
       01 MX REDEFINES M PIC X(2).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           ADD 1 TO N GIVING M
           DISPLAY "M=" M
           IF N = 123 DISPLAY "EQ" ELSE DISPLAY "NE" END-IF
           IF MX = X"124C" DISPLAY "C" ELSE DISPLAY "NOT-C" END-IF
           STOP RUN.
c5-packed-unsigned-sign-nibble.note: The oracle has no NUMPROC flag in plain -std=ibm; it reads F as positive and stores C, the NOPFD answer. The register's PFD claim (the same with preferred signs only) is not exercised by this probe.

c12-random-sequence.question: FUNCTION RANDOM(7), RANDOM with no argument, RANDOM(7) again, RANDOM(0): does the same seed restart the same sequence (IBM: yes, but the numbers themselves are IBM's own generator)
c12-random-sequence.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P12.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 R1 PIC 9V9(6).
       01 R2 PIC 9V9(6).
       01 R3 PIC 9V9(6).
       01 R4 PIC 9V9(6).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE R1 = FUNCTION RANDOM(7)
           COMPUTE R2 = FUNCTION RANDOM
           COMPUTE R3 = FUNCTION RANDOM(7)
           COMPUTE R4 = FUNCTION RANDOM(0)
           DISPLAY "R1=" R1
           DISPLAY "R2=" R2
           DISPLAY "R3=" R3
           DISPLAY "R4=" R4
           STOP RUN.
c12-random-sequence.note: The numbers are glibc's rand() / RAND_MAX; z/OS will differ by design (register C12: the numbers DIFFER). The restart property and the unseeded-start-is-seed-zero rule are what a z/OS run can confirm.

f1-indexed-file-status.compile_options: default (a VSAM KSDS behind the KFILE DD, 4-byte key at offset 0)
f1-indexed-file-status.question: FILE STATUS after OPEN OUTPUT, a WRITE, a WRITE of the same key, a READ of a missing key, a READ of a present key, START GREATER THAN and READ NEXT past the last record: IBM Table 34 gives 00, 22, 23 and 10
f1-indexed-file-status.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P1F.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT KF ASSIGN TO KFILE
               ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
               ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC
               RECORD KEY IS KF-KEY
               FILE STATUS IS FS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD KF.
       01 KF-REC.
          05 KF-KEY PIC X(4).
          05 KF-VAL PIC X(4).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 FS PIC XX.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           OPEN OUTPUT KF
           DISPLAY "OPEN=" FS
           MOVE "A001DATA" TO KF-REC
           WRITE KF-REC
           DISPLAY "W1=" FS
           WRITE KF-REC
           DISPLAY "W2=" FS
           MOVE "B002DATA" TO KF-REC
           WRITE KF-REC
           DISPLAY "W3=" FS
           CLOSE KF
           OPEN I-O KF
           MOVE "Z999" TO KF-KEY
           READ KF
           DISPLAY "R1=" FS
           MOVE "A001" TO KF-KEY
           READ KF
           DISPLAY "R2=" FS
           MOVE "A001" TO KF-KEY
           START KF KEY IS GREATER THAN KF-KEY
           DISPLAY "S1=" FS
           READ KF NEXT
           DISPLAY "N1=" FS
           READ KF NEXT
           DISPLAY "N2=" FS
           CLOSE KF
           STOP RUN.
f1-indexed-file-status.note: F1's ASSUMED part is that GnuCOBOL's Berkeley DB file raises each code in the same situation as VSAM. Needs an empty KSDS defined by IDCAMS before the run (the OPEN OUTPUT of a VSAM file needs it empty, or REUSE). The order of two applicable checks (21 vs 22) is not probed.

f3-variable-record-length.question: Records of 5, 10 and 7 bytes written to a variable-length sequential file and read back: the length each READ reports in the DEPENDING ON item and the status at end of file
f3-variable-record-length.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P3F.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT VF ASSIGN TO VFILE
               ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL
               FILE STATUS IS FS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD VF
           RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 1 TO 20 CHARACTERS
               DEPENDING ON LEN.
       01 VF-REC PIC X(20).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 FS PIC XX.
       01 LEN PIC 9(4) COMP.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           OPEN OUTPUT VF
           MOVE 5 TO LEN
           MOVE "AAAAA" TO VF-REC
           WRITE VF-REC
           MOVE 10 TO LEN
           MOVE "BBBBBBBBBB" TO VF-REC
           WRITE VF-REC
           MOVE 7 TO LEN
           MOVE "CCCCCCC" TO VF-REC
           WRITE VF-REC
           CLOSE VF
           OPEN INPUT VF
           PERFORM 3 TIMES
               READ VF
               DISPLAY "L=" LEN " FS=" FS
           END-PERFORM
           READ VF
           DISPLAY "END FS=" FS
           CLOSE VF
           STOP RUN.
f3-variable-record-length.note: Tests the content and length the program sees, which is what the register compares; the oracle frames records its own way and z/OS adds a 4-byte RDW the program never sees (F3). The DD must be RECFM=VB with LRECL at least 24; the ASSIGN name is VFILE.

l3-no-value-working-storage.compile_options: default; run once with LE STORAGE(NONE,NONE,NONE,0K) (IBM default) and once with STORAGE(00)
l3-no-value-working-storage.question: DISPLAY of WORKING-STORAGE items that have no VALUE clause: alphanumeric, unsigned and signed zoned, packed and binary. IBM leaves the contents undefined (LE STORAGE decides)
l3-no-value-working-storage.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P3L.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 A PIC X(4).
       01 N PIC 9(4).
       01 S PIC S9(4).
       01 P PIC S9(5) COMP-3.
       01 B PIC S9(4) COMP.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           DISPLAY "A=[" A "]"
           DISPLAY "N=" N
           DISPLAY "S=" S
           DISPLAY "P=" P
           DISPLAY "B=" B
           STOP RUN.
l3-no-value-working-storage.note: The oracle gives spaces and zeros; z/OS shows whatever the storage held, so the expected outcome is a recorded difference (verdict differs), not a match. Record the STORAGE option in the options field.

c6-float-move-to-edited.question: MOVE COMP-1 1.875 to -(5)9.99: IBM rounds a float moved to an edited item (1.88), the oracle truncates
c6-float-move-to-edited.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PA.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 G COMP-1 VALUE 1.875.
       01 E PIC -(5)9.99.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE G TO E
           DISPLAY "E=" E
           STOP RUN.
c6-float-move-to-edited.note: The oracle shows 1.87; the det port follows IBM and gives 1.88 (#4688). The z/OS result decides.

c6-compound-float-compute.question: COMPUTE R1 = ((FA / 2) * (0.5 + F4)), FA COMP-1 5, F4 COMP-2 4: IBM evaluates the whole expression in floating point (11.25)
c6-compound-float-compute.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 FA COMP-1 VALUE 5.
       01 F4 COMP-2 VALUE 4.
       01 R1 PIC S9(7)V99.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE R1 = ((FA / 2) * (0.5 + F4))
           DISPLAY "R1=" R1
           STOP RUN.
c6-compound-float-compute.note: The oracle evaluates in decimal and stores 0 (#4688); the det port gives 11.25 in long HFP. The z/OS result decides.

c6-float-zero-add-to-packed.question: ADD a COMP-2 zero to a COMP-3 0.68: IBM runs the statement in floating point, so the packed value goes through HFP and may store 0.67
c6-float-zero-add-to-packed.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PC.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 FZ2 COMP-2 VALUE 0.
       01 R4 PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3 VALUE 0.68.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           ADD FZ2 TO R4
           DISPLAY "R4=" R4
           STOP RUN.
c6-float-zero-add-to-packed.note: The oracle keeps 0.68; the det port gives 0.67 (#4688, ASSUMED truncation). The z/OS result decides.

c10-zoned-sign-zone-after-value-zero-and.question: Last byte of a signed zoned S9(3) after VALUE ZERO and after INITIALIZE: the preferred positive sign C (X"C0") on IBM, the unsigned zone F (plain digit) on GnuCOBOL
c10-zoned-sign-zone-after-value-zero-and.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P10.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 Z1 PIC S9(3) VALUE ZERO.
       01 Z1X REDEFINES Z1 PIC X(3).
       01 Z2 PIC S9(3).
       01 Z2X REDEFINES Z2 PIC X(3).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           INITIALIZE Z2
           IF Z1X(3:1) = "0"
              DISPLAY "VALUE=PLAIN"
           ELSE
              DISPLAY "VALUE=SIGNED"
           END-IF
           IF Z2X(3:1) = "0"
              DISPLAY "INIT=PLAIN"
           ELSE
              DISPLAY "INIT=SIGNED"
           END-IF
           STOP RUN.
c10-zoned-sign-zone-after-value-zero-and.note: Expected z/OS: VALUE=SIGNED, INIT=SIGNED (C zone). Register C10: the same positive value, different bytes; the comparator tolerates it per declared dataset.

c16-comp5-one-and-two-digit-size.question: A PIC S9(2) COMP-5 item: LENGTH OF (halfword, 2, on IBM; one byte in GnuCOBOL) and MOVE 99999 into it (COMP-5 keeps the halfword's capacity: -31073 on IBM)
c16-comp5-one-and-two-digit-size.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P16.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 C2 PIC S9(2) COMP-5.
       01 LEN PIC 9(2).
       01 NUM PIC -9(5).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE LEN = LENGTH OF C2
           DISPLAY "LEN=" LEN
           MOVE 99999 TO C2
           MOVE C2 TO NUM
           DISPLAY "VAL=" NUM
           STOP RUN.
c16-comp5-one-and-two-digit-size.note: Expected z/OS: LEN=02, VAL=-31073 (register C16, measured values for the oracle in its page).

c7-comp5-byte-order.question: A PIC S9(4) COMP-5 item holding 1, read through a PIC X(2) REDEFINES: X"0001" (big-endian, z/OS) or X"0100" (little-endian, x86 GnuCOBOL)
c7-comp5-byte-order.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P7.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 N PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE 1.
       01 NX REDEFINES N PIC X(2).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           IF NX = X"0001"
              DISPLAY "BIG"
           ELSE
              IF NX = X"0100"
                 DISPLAY "LITTLE"
              ELSE
                 DISPLAY "OTHER"
              END-IF
           END-IF
           STOP RUN.
c7-comp5-byte-order.note: Expected z/OS: BIG. The det translator refuses a program that observes COMP-5 bytes (C7), so no burned program rests on this.

c9-pointer-size.question: LENGTH OF a USAGE POINTER item: 4 on z/OS, 8 in GnuCOBOL on x86-64
c9-pointer-size.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P9.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 P1 USAGE POINTER.
       01 LEN PIC 9(2).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE LEN = LENGTH OF P1
           DISPLAY "LEN=" LEN
           STOP RUN.
c9-pointer-size.note: Expected z/OS: LEN=04. CBSA reaches only NULL pointers (register C9).

c17-initialize-replacing-table.question: INITIALIZE G REPLACING NUMERIC BY 5 where G is a table of a PIC XX and a PIC 99 item (XX is a category REPLACING does not name): IBM leaves occurrence 2 as it was (AB); GnuCOBOL copies occurrence 1 over it (spaces)
c17-initialize-replacing-table.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P17.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 G.
          05 GT OCCURS 3.
             10 GA PIC XX VALUE SPACE.
             10 GN PIC 99 VALUE ZERO.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE 'AB' TO GA(2)
           INITIALIZE G REPLACING NUMERIC BY 5
           DISPLAY "GA2=" GA(2)
           DISPLAY "GN2=" GN(2)
           STOP RUN.
c17-initialize-replacing-table.note: Expected z/OS: GA2=AB, GN2=05. Register C17; the port follows IBM and stops by name when occurrences differ. Burned reach: CardDemo COPAUA0C 8400-UPDATE-SUMMARY.

d1-ascii-vs-ebcdic-order.question: Native collating order of three pairs: a vs A, 1 vs a, space vs 1. ASCII: a>A, 1<a, space<1; EBCDIC: a<A, 1>a, space<1
d1-ascii-vs-ebcdic-order.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. P1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 LA PIC X VALUE "a".
       01 UA PIC X VALUE "A".
       01 DG PIC X VALUE "1".
       01 SP PIC X VALUE SPACE.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           IF LA > UA
              DISPLAY "LOWER>UPPER"
           ELSE
              DISPLAY "LOWER<UPPER"
           END-IF
           IF DG > LA
              DISPLAY "DIGIT>LOWER"
           ELSE
              DISPLAY "DIGIT<LOWER"
           END-IF
           IF SP < DG
              DISPLAY "SPACE<DIGIT"
           ELSE
              DISPLAY "SPACE>DIGIT"
           END-IF
           STOP RUN.
d1-ascii-vs-ebcdic-order.note: Expected z/OS: LOWER<UPPER, DIGIT>LOWER, SPACE<DIGIT. Keys and comparisons are not audited for burned reach (register D1).
